title: Alleged Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator asks court to revoke detention order
summary: According to court filings, Melody Bryant was not the only one who initially failed to recognize killer Jesse Van Rootselaar was "genuinely dangerous." The motion says records show the shooter shared…

image.caption: Melody Bryant, who was charged under the name James Cody Bryant in October, is seen in a court sketch. The alleged co-conspirator of Tumbler Ridge school shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar has applied to revoke a U.S. detention order. (Lois Silver)

blocks.text: An American accused of helping Jesse Van Rootselaar plan the Tumbler Ridge massacre has filed an application to get out of jail, asking a Seattle court judge to review and revoke a previous detention order.

A magistrate judge ordered the detention of Melody Bryant, who was charged under the name James Cody Bryant in October, after the government argued the accused would be a danger to the public if released.
Bryant, 30, is charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country, an offence that carries a maximum sentence of life in prison and a $250,000 US fine. She has pleaded not guilty.
The trial was originally scheduled to begin next month, but has been moved to December 2027.

Her lawyers say in court filings that their client is not a danger to the public and should be released with conditions. They say at the time of the Oct. 13 detention hearing, they had not yet received discovery documents and could not properly respond to the government's argument.
U.S. resident allegedly gave advice, money to Tumbler Ridge shooter
On Feb. 10, Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother Jennifer Strang, 39, and half-brother Emmett Jacobs, 11, in their home.

She then drove to Tumbler Ridge Secondary School where she gunned down Abel Mwansa, 12, Zoey Benoit, 12, Ezekiel Schofield, 13, Kylie Smith, 12, Ticaria Lampert, 12, and educational assistant Shannda Aviugana-Durand, 39.
Two other students were shot but survived.

items: Alleged co-conspirator in Tumbler Ridge shooting has trial delayed until December 2027

blocks.text: In their 33-page motion for revocation of detention order filed last week, Bryant's lawyers say the case is based mainly on nearly 74,000 individual texts between Van Rootselaar and Bryant on messaging platform Discord, sent between Aug. 1 and Feb. 10, 2025.
Approximately two-thirds of those messages, numbering 47,750, are from Van Rootselaar to Bryant.
Bryant's lawyers say while some of their clients messages "may be tasteless and, in retrospect, were ill considered" they are protected by the First Amendment.

"For better or worse, the First Amendment also protects their debate about whether a school shooting or attack on a crowd would be more likely to make someone infamous, even if the government tries to recast that conversation as 'tactical advice,'" said the Nov. 18 motion filed by Bryant's lawyers.
Discord messages reveal Tumbler Ridge shooter, U.S. resident planning attack
The motion includes excerpts of chats between Bryant and Van Rootselaar, including one on Christmas Day 2025 used to show instances where Bryant refused to engage in violent rants.
"I hope I ruin everyone's life when I do my plan. I want nobody to recover … whenever I say some mentally ill ahh stuff I feel like u stop messaging me lol…," wrote Van Rootselaar.
Bryant wrote back, "Harder to reply to."
The court filings say, for part of the six-month period where Bryant spoke daily to Van Rootselaar, the shooter's "plan" was clearly a fantasy because Van Rootselaar did not have access to guns.
"Eventually, however, the RCMP returned her seized weapons."
Seized guns used in shooting: documents

According to the court filings, Bryant was not the only one who initially failed to recognize Van Rootselaar was "genuinely dangerous." The motion says records show the shooter shared her plans widely and had even "received encouragement from other online contacts."
She got tactical advice from ChatGPT, family and friends bought her ammunition, even after she was released from psychiatric hospitalization and the RCMP, according to the motion.

items: Tumbler Ridge shooter stole guns from family safe as part of attack plans, new court filings reveal
RCMP says it still won't share more details on firearms used in Tumbler Ridge shooting

blocks.text: Bryant's lawyers add that the RCMP had removed, and then later returned, Van Rootselaar's guns, "one of which had been altered to enable more rapid firing."
"In fact, the RCMP apparently returned the gun with the alteration intact. Van Rootselaar then used the altered firearm in the shooting," said the Nov. 18 motion.

Days after the Tumbler Ridge shooting, RCMP said a long gun and modified rifle were seized from the school, and two firearms including a shotgun were seized among a number of other firearms at the residence.

The shotgun is believed to have been used in the homicides at the home and had not been previously seized by police. Mounties also said they had not previously seized the main firearm used in the school shooting and its origins are unknown.
Report details Tumbler Ridge shooter’s alleged ChatGPT interactions
Bryant's lawyers say their client promised not to snitch on the shooter because Bryant believed it would result in violence, and accelerate the shooter's homicidal plans.

"While it is horrifying in retrospect to imagine that Ms. Bryant might have stopped Van Rootselaar from committing a terrible crime if she had contacted the police, it is undisputed that the law provided no affirmative duty to do so," said the motion.
The court filings said in the past Bryant was able to talk Van Rootselaar out of committing a crime, and did not understand violence was imminent.
A memorial for the victims of a school shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School is pictured on Feb. 11, 2026. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
Bryant's lawyers say the shooter viewed Bryant as "a nonjudgemental sounding board for ruminating about her mental illness," and that Bryant helped her resist her urges.
The defence included chats to illustrate that.
In an undated message, Van Rootselaar writes "I **really** wanna shoot ppl, idk what to do with that feeling lmao. Like how do I relieve that? I can't talk about it much even."
"Yeah I think most would snitch," replies Bryant.
"Except for you who silently discourage it and a few others who openly encourage it," responds Van Rootselaar.
Government distorted evidence: defence

Bryant's lawyers say the U.S. government's 41-page complaint against their client is "replete with distortions" and includes rearranged text messages made to appear that Bryant was agreeing to help the shooter build a bomb.

The motion for revocation of detention order says the conversation included in the complaint showing Bryant agreeing to pay for a lighter needed to make a bomb occurred over two days and in between 225 messages.

"In fact, nowhere in the complete chats does Van Rootselaar say that she needs a lighter for the bomb. Nowhere does Bryant offer to provide Van Rootselaar a lighter for that purpose," said the court filing.
U.S. resident met Tumbler Ridge shooter on Omegle: FBI
Bryant's lawyers say the decision to piece the texts together "seems designed to lead the magistrate judge to make a false inference."
They say while Bryant agreed to watch a livestream and if possible distribute it, she did not agree with Van Rootselaar's plans to kill people.
The motion says the fact that law enforcement left Bryant in the community for seven months after reviewing her Discord chats shows she does not pose a danger.
The magistrate judge concluded Bryant suffers from a "deeply rooted" mental illness and substance abuse history.

Bryant's lawyers say that is not true. Bryant is currently being treated for gender dysphoria and had previously been prescribed medication for anxiety but no longer takes that drug, according to the motion.
The U.S. state's attorney's response is due Wednesday, then a judge will decide if Bryant should be released.
